name: Baladi
notes: Baladi style pack (Doc 04 template, genuinely solo — baladi is a home dance before it is anything else). BALADI means 'of the country, of the homeland, local' — and the dance carries the word's whole weight: when rural Egyptians moved into Cairo's neighborhoods in the early 20th century, the countryside's dance moved into apartments, weddings, and rooftops and became the city's most honest dance — earthy, heavy-hipped, humorous, danced for family and for yourself. This pack holds the relationship this app's raqs sharqi pack points back to: RAQS SHARQI IS BALADI IN AN EVENING GOWN — the stage form is the daughter, the home form is the mother, and training baladi first is training the truth under the polish. Credits kept loud: the BINT AL-BALAD ('daughter of the homeland') character — proud, warm, quick-witted — is the dance's soul, and the baladi queens who put it on stage without losing the apartment in it are credited by name: FIFI ABDOU, whose baladi ruled Cairo for decades, and SOUHAIR ZAKI, beloved as the most baladi of the golden-era stars. The BALADI PROGRESSION (awwady) — solo accordion improvisation answered by the dancer, the tak-tak conversation, then the full drums arriving — is the form's masterwork structure and rides in this app's Rhythm Trainer. Learn from Egyptian teachers wherever possible; baladi's home is a living culture, not a costume.

seasons.finale: Film yourself dancing baladi in your own home, comfortable clothes, one song — the apartment IS the venue.
Film the heavy hipwork — drops, lifts, and the low shimmy — grounded and unhurried for one full song.
Film the baladi walk — small steps carrying big hips — traveling your room like it's a Cairo rooftop.
Film a full baladi progression: answer the accordion alone, ride the tak-tak, arrive with the drums.
Take a class with an Egyptian teacher (in person or online) and bring one correction back into your practice journal.

attributes.name: Heavy-hip control L2
attributes.test: 60s alternating slow hip drops and lifts with bent knees, weight sunk — controlled at half speed, which is harder

attributes.name: Taqsim listening L1
attributes.test: listen to one accordion taqsim eyes closed and mark every phrase-end with a breath — the dance answers phrases, not beats

nodes.name: The baladi progression — the form's masterwork
checkpoints: the classic arc (often called awwady): a solo accordion improvises freely — the dancer answers alone; the tabla enters with the tak-tak conversation; the full rhythm arrives and the dance blooms — one structure, three chapters; the groove is in this app's Rhythm Trainer
the progression is a dialogue, not a playlist: the dancer's job in chapter one is LISTENING made visible
find three recorded baladi progressions and learn their shapes before dancing them — the map before the road

nodes.name: Accordion, tabla & the Cairo sound
checkpoints: baladi's sound is early-20th-century Cairo mixing itself: the European accordion retuned to Egypt's quarter-tones, the tabla underneath, mizmar and saxophone visiting
the quarter-tones are the homesickness in the sound — an accordion bent to speak Arabic; learn to hear the notes between the piano's notes
the tabla's dum (deep, center) and tak (sharp, rim) are the dance's own vocabulary — your hips already know which is which

nodes.name: Baladi — the word and the migration
checkpoints: BALADI means 'of the country, of the homeland, local' — pride and earth in one word; when rural Egyptians moved to Cairo in the early 20th century, the countryside's dance became the city's home dance
it lives in apartments, weddings, and rooftops — danced for family, for joy, for yourself; the stage came later and never replaced the living room
the BINT AL-BALAD — the 'daughter of the homeland' — is the dance's character: proud, warm, quick-witted, entirely unimpressed by pretension

nodes.name: The baladi queens — and the evening gown
checkpoints: RAQS SHARQI IS BALADI IN AN EVENING GOWN: the stage form this app's raqs pack teaches is the daughter; baladi is the mother — train the truth under the polish

the queens who staged it without losing the apartment in it: FIFI ABDOU, whose baladi ruled Cairo for decades, and SOUHAIR ZAKI, beloved as the most baladi of the golden-era stars — watch them and see the living room survive the spotlight
learn from Egyptian teachers wherever possible — baladi is a living home culture, and the accent matters

nodes.name: The baladi posture — sunk and easy
checkpoints: weight SUNK: knees soft, pelvis heavy, feet flat and friendly with the floor — baladi sits into the ground where raqs sharqi lifts out of it
arms relaxed and low by default — framing the hips loosely, never presenting like a stage
the face is home: amused, warm, unperformed — dance like nobody paid a ticket, because at baladi's heart nobody did
mistakes: lifting into stage posture (that's the daughter's habit — the mother stays grounded)

nodes.name: Heavy hipwork — drops, lifts & the low shimmy
checkpoints: hip drops and lifts with WEIGHT — each one lands like a word said plainly; baladi hips are heavy, deliberate, and completely unhurried
the low shimmy: loose-kneed, earthy, layered over the sunk posture — a rumble, not a glitter
accent the dum with the drop: the tabla's deep note and your hip agree on gravity
slower is harder and slower is the style — drill everything at half speed until it's honest
mistakes: polishing the hips into stage smoothness (baladi keeps the grain in the wood)

nodes.name: The baladi walk
checkpoints: small flat steps carrying big hip movement — the walk travels a living room, not a stage diagonal
each step lets the hip settle fully before the next — arrival over trajectory, always
walk a slow circle marking dums with hip drops — the classic practice loop, and a complete dance by itself

nodes.name: Answering the taqsim
checkpoints: chapter one of the progression: the accordion improvises and you answer — slow undulations, held shapes, hips tracing the melody's rise and fall with no drum to hide behind
move ON the phrases: begin when the accordion begins a thought, settle when it breathes — the skill is visible listening
less is the mastery: one honest hip circle that follows the melody beats eight that ignore it

nodes.name: Riding the build to the drums
checkpoints: chapters two and three: the tak-tak conversation sharpens your accents, then the full rhythm arrives and the dance blooms — grow WITH the arrangement, never ahead of it
the bloom is earned: if chapter one was honest listening, chapter three's joy reads as arrival instead of aerobics
practice the full arc with a recorded progression weekly — it is the form's complete sentence

nodes.name: The rooftop set — filmed
checkpoints: film one full baladi progression: taqsim answered alone, tak-tak ridden, drums arrived-at — home clothes, home room, full presence
the grain check on review: did the polish creep in? re-film sunk lower and 20% slower if it did
say it on camera: baladi, 'of the homeland', Egypt — and name one queen whose clips you studied

nodes.name: The living culture
checkpoints: take class with an Egyptian teacher — in person or online, the accent transmits things video can't; the raqs sharqi world's baladi workshops are the standard doorway
if a wedding or hafla invites you to the floor, dance the home dance at home volume — baladi's etiquette is joining, not performing
carry the relationship forward: when someone praises your raqs sharqi someday, tell them about the mother

teachers.name: Souhair Zaki — the most baladi of the golden era
